synthesis: All three linear baselines tie at 0.6054, so the model family doesn't matter. The gain over the mean-response baseline (0.4755) comes almost entirely from a rescaled mean response plus a target indicator. Predictions are shrunk to about half the true delta scale (ratio 0.506), and the worst perturbations probably have target-specific responses that the global mean cannot capture. The obvious next lever is perturbation-specific signal: what links the target gene to gene g, through co-expression, the prior network, gene modules, or similar training perturbations.

hypotheses.title: Target-gene co-expression in controls
hypotheses.hypothesis: Adding the control-cell correlation between the target gene and gene g will raise pearson_delta above 0.6054.
hypotheses.rationale: Knocking out a regulator should shift the genes that co-vary with it in unperturbed cells. The sign and size of their correlation should predict the direction and size of the response. This gives a signal specific to each perturbation, which mean_response lacks.

new_feature.name: target_coexpression
new_feature.description: Pearson correlation across control cells between expression of p's target gene and gene g, multiplied by -1 to reflect a KO (0 if the target is not measured)
new_feature.implementation_hint: Compute the gene-gene correlation matrix C from control cells (optionally log1p first). For row (p,g): feature = -C[target(p), g]. Set the diagonal to 0.

hypotheses.title: Nearest-neighbour perturbation response transfer
hypotheses.hypothesis: A weighted average of training deltas from the perturbations whose targets are most co-expressed with p's target will predict delta better than the global mean response.
hypotheses.rationale: Perturbing genes in the same program should give similar responses. Transferring leave-one-out responses from similar targets gives a prediction tailored to each perturbation.

new_feature.name: knn_response_transfer
new_feature.description: For (p,g): weighted mean of delta[q,g] over the k training perturbations q != p whose targets are most similar to p's target, by absolute control co-expression
new_feature.implementation_hint: Similarity between target genes = |corr| of control expression (or cosine on the gene's correlation profile). Take the top-k training perturbations, excluding p, and weight their deltas by similarity. Fall back to mean_response if all weights are 0.

hypotheses.title: Prior-network signed downstream effect
hypotheses.hypothesis: A diffusion score from the target through the prior regulatory network will add signal on top of the baseline features.
hypotheses.rationale: In a synthetic GRN, a KO propagates mostly along the true edges. The prior network (252 edges) probably overlaps them, so the signed propagation from the target should predict which genes move.

new_feature.name: network_diffusion_effect
new_feature.description: Signed propagated effect on gene g of setting p's target to -1, using the prior network adjacency (sum over paths up to length L with decay)
new_feature.implementation_hint: Build a directed signed adjacency A[src,dst]=weight. Start with x0 = -e_target. Compute effect = sum_{l=1..L} beta^(l-1) * (A^T)^l x0, with L=3 and beta=0.5. Feature = effect[g]. Optionally also report the undirected version.

hypotheses.title: Interaction of mean response with target co-module membership
hypotheses.hypothesis: Interacting mean_response with whether g shares a gene-set module with p's target will capture module-specific amplification and help the worst perturbations.
hypotheses.rationale: Untested and high-variance. Responses may be strongly concentrated in the target's module, and a gated mean response could also fix the shrinkage of the delta scale.

new_feature.name: same_module_x_mean_response
new_feature.description: mean_response[g] multiplied by 1 if g and p's target share any gene_sets module, else 0; also include the raw same_module indicator
new_feature.implementation_hint: Map each gene to its set of modules. same = len(mod[g] & mod[target]) > 0. Output two columns: same_module and same_module*mean_response (mean_response leave-one-out as existing).
